3. ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS OF THE PROPOSED ACTION
3.1 CONSTRUCTION
3.1.1 Land Features and Uses
The principal land uses within the proposed project area consist of commercial timber production and limited low-density outdoor recreation activities. Approximately 370 acres required for the proposed upper reservoir and associated project structures and 95 acres required for the access road and switchyard would be removed from present use during the life of the project. In addition, about 40 acres of nearby lands would be temporarily cleared and used for general construction activities and as a construction spoil area; these areas would be sloped and revegetated after construction is completed. Another 315 acres would be required for construction of the project transmission line. These lands would be reseeded to assume an essentially natural condition, consistent with overhead clearance requirements. About 505 acres would be permanently removed from timber production. The most commercially valuable timber species affected would be shortleaf pine, oaks, and hickories. Finally, a narrow 31-mile-long corridor extending from the vicinity of lower Whitewater Falls to Table Rock State Park would be cleared of undergrowth and maintained as a hiking trail during the life of the project.
There have been no commercial mineral finds to date in the area, and no significant mining activity is foreseen.
The project should have a minimal impact upon public health and safety due to its remote location and the Applicant's intention to fence the entire upper reservoir area to prohibit public use of the area.
Construction of the Bad Creek Project would result in some temporary disruption of traffic patterns in the immediate area as a result of the relocation of a portion of State Road 171 made necessary by construction of the upper reservoir. Traffic may also be slowed and impeded during construction by the travel of heavy equipment and trucks along the steep grades typical of the roads near the proposed project area. The construction activities would have no impact on aviation patterns within the area.
